comments.comment: Your explanation of how money is created around 11:00 is far from the true actually.   Truly, central banks such as the Fed can create money from thin air (ex nihilo) but they're not the only ones. Retail banks ("consumer" banks) also have this ability and that's precisely what distinguishes them from other financial institutions such as insurance or investment firms.  However, central and retail banks create 2 different types of money. Central banks create "central" money which can only be exchanged between these retail banks. Instead, retail banks create fiduciary ("fiat") money which is used by everyone (consumers, companies etc). This money creation happens when a cresit is created. Retail banks do not need to have the funds to make a credit. Instead, money is created at that moment. When the Credit is paid back, the debt is erased and the money destroyed.   Central banks can to some extent control how retail banks create money, but they actually not have that much control (at least in the Euro zone).  See more detail about this (Credit theory of money) https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_theory_of_money
